what: On a horizontal-scroll page, the video or photo of a one-screen-wide section first shows only as a narrow vertical window, with half-width 115px, top 300px, and bottom 10.4% of the screen subtracted. As the section enters from the right, the window arrives ahead of the section and reaches the screen center (lead −(section width/2 + 115 + 30)px → 0). Standing there, while the next screen is scrolled past, the top and bottom go to 0 and the half-width opens straight to half the screen, becoming full screen (tied to scroll, no curve). When it starts opening, is-fx-open is added to the section so the previous screen’s text can be erased

options.gap: Right margin of the window (px) — added to the lead, default 30
options.top: Initial top window cover (px), default 300 — in the source, the height of the poem block head on the previous screen
options.bottom: Initial cover below window (ratio of section height), default .104
options.min · aspect: Turn-on screen (min width px · max aspect ratio), default 782 · 3/1 — outside it, the picture fills the frame as is
options.[data-fx-part=media]: Picture box viewed through the window (required) — video·img inside fill and cover it fully

note: Measured by horizontal scroll position (scrollX) — place it inside a horizontal scroller like side-scroll-page. The section needs at least one screen of a previous section on its left, as right after the hero, so the window starts at the right edge. Hiding the previous screen’s text is the consumer’s css: section:has(.is-fx-open) .intro { opacity: 0; transition: opacity .8s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) }

from.where: index.html .dk-window (Hero: the video in the narrow right-hand window → fills the whole screen before the table of contents. Original js-scroll-mask — baseWidth 115em · baseX 30em · mask-top is the head of the poem block, mask-bottom is 104/1000 of the screen). The site’s single copy does the same calculation in index.js windowMask
